title: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services
path: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services

headings.title: Introduction to Healthcare Delivery Systems in Nigeria
headings.content: The healthcare delivery system in Nigeria is structured into three distinct tiers: primary, secondary, and tertiary. This tiered framework aims to make health services accessible to everyone, regardless of where they live. Responsibility for these levels is shared among the federal, state, and local governments. The primary level sits at the grassroots, managed mostly by local government authorities. The secondary level provides specialized care at the state level, while the tertiary tier handles complex medical cases under federal control. Understanding this architecture helps nurses navigate patient placement, resource allocation, and referral systems effectively.

headings.title: Primary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Primary health care (PHC) is the first point of contact for individuals seeking medical attention. These facilities are located within rural and urban communities.

- **Health Posts**: The most basic units, staffed by community health workers, providing very basic health education and first aid.
- **Health Clinics**: Offer routine outpatient care, immunizations, and antenatal services.
- **Primary Health Centres (PHCs)**: Comprehensive primary facilities equipped for normal deliveries, basic laboratory checks, and minor treatments.

Nurses working here focus heavily on disease prevention, health promotion, and community diagnosis.

headings.title: Secondary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Secondary health facilities provide specialized services to patients referred from primary care centers. They typically take the form of general hospitals, comprehensive health centers, or state specialist hospitals located in urban centers and local government headquarters.

These facilities feature distinct departments including internal medicine, general surgery, pediatrics, and obstetrics and gynecology. They possess diagnostic laboratories, blood bank services, and operating theaters. Patients who require admission, specialized medical evaluation, or surgical operations that exceed the capacity of a primary health center are managed here by medical officers, general practitioners, and specialized nursing personnel.

headings.title: Tertiary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Tertiary health facilities represent the apex of the healthcare delivery system. These include teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, and specialized research institutes such as orthopedic or psychiatric hospitals. They are equipped with advanced technology and highly specialized personnel like consultants, sub-specialists, and specialized nurses.

Care at this level involves complex medical interventions, advanced diagnostics, and long-term rehabilitation. Beyond patient care, tertiary institutions serve as training grounds for doctors, nurses, and other allied health professionals, while also driving medical research.

headings.title: Social Services and Community Support
headings.content:
Healthcare extends beyond medical treatment into social services that address the broader determinants of health. Medical social workers and community health nurses collaborate to support vulnerable populations, including orphans, the elderly, indigent patients, and persons with disabilities.

- **Financial Aid**: Helping indigent patients access hospital fee waivers or charity funds.
- **Rehabilitation Support**: Connecting patients with vocational training and physical therapy resources.
- **Counseling Services**: Providing psychological support for chronic illnesses, terminal diagnosis, or social trauma.

Integrating social services ensures that patients recover not just physically, but also within a supportive family and community environment.

headings.title: Inter-Referral Pathways and Continuity of Care
headings.content:
A functional referral system ensures patients move smoothly between different levels of healthcare based on their clinical needs. Referral can be upward, when a primary clinic sends a complicated obstetric case to a general hospital, or downward, when a stable patient from a teaching hospital is sent back to a primary health center for follow-up and drug refills.

Effective referral requires clear documentation, a formal referral letter, and direct communication between healthcare providers. Without this structured pathway, patients experience delays, overcrowding at tertiary centers, and fragmented care that compromises clinical outcomes.

headings.title: The Role of Nurses Across Different Facility Levels
headings.content:
Nursing roles adapt to fit the scope and demands of each healthcare tier. At the primary level, community health nurses act as educators, immunizers, and home visitors, managing common ailments and promoting hygiene. Secondary level nurses function largely as general ward nurses, handling acute admissions, surgical preparations, and routine inpatient monitoring.

In tertiary facilities, nurses often specialize in areas like intensive care, nephrology, oncology, or neonatology, engaging in advanced clinical decision-making and clinical research. Across all levels, nurses remain the continuous link in patient advocacy, safety, and coordination of care.
